1.2 vérification du système

  1. On installe les commandes de base

  2. verifier le chemin R et Python :

on vérifie que les chemins vers R et python fonctionne. J’utilise un environement virtuel dans visual_code, il faut donc entre sur d’être dans le bon environement virtuel. Certains packages de R repose sur des fonctions en python, elles mêmes contenues dans des packages en python. Choisir la bonne version de python peut donc avoir son importance selon le package que l’on utilise. Ici on travail en 3.10.

(mais peut-être 3.9 pourrait être plus adéquat.)

system("python --version", intern = TRUE)
## [1] "Python 3.8.20"
system("which python", intern = TRUE)
## [1] "/usr/bin/python"
system("which R", intern = TRUE) 
## [1] "/usr/bin/R"

On indique sur quel dossier on va travailler

2.1 Load packages

On choisit le serveur hébergeant le dépot Cran.

# Set CRAN mirror interactively to ETH Zurich (mirror 63)
# chooseCRANmirror() and choose 63 for switzerland e.g. 
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://stat.ethz.ch/CRAN/"))

On installe les packages necessaires

les packages permettent des traitements diverses de l’information :

  • Text Analysis & Processing
    • Text Mining & NLP (quanteda, tm, stopwords, udpipe, tidytext)
    • Text Prediction (sbo)
    • String Manipulation (stringr, stringi, magrittr)
    • Collostructional Analysis (collostructions)
  • Data Analysis & Transformation
    • Data Processing (dplyr)
    • Sparse Matrices (Matrix)
    • Information Theory & Feature Selection (infotheo)
  • Topic Modeling & Clustering
    • Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) (topicmodels, LDAvis, ldatuning)
    • Dimensionality Reduction (tsne)
  • Network & Graph Analysis
    • Network Structures & Graphs (igraph, network, sna)
  • Data Visualization
    • General Data Visualization (ggplot2)
    • Dendrogram Visualization (ggdendro)
    • Word Clouds (wordcloud, wordcloud2)
    • Color Palettes (RColorBrewer)
  • Utility Tools
    • Local Web Server & Reporting (servr)

options(max.print=1000)

3 lemmatisation

Les analyses de réseau en latin demande une lemmatisation du corpus, or ce procedé est complexifié par l’état de langue des texte du 16eme siècle.

Concernant la lemmatisation, on utilise une approche 1. des données annotés automiquement par Pyrrha , augumentée et corrigée à la main.

  1. il existe d’autres méthodes à tester dans un second temps

    • automatiser la lemmatisation avec CLTK:

      -Un très bon tutorial : Introduction to NLP and CLTK (Latin NLP with Python) : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OtxC44b1rws

    • travailler sur le topic-modelling LatinBert

Dans notre cas, les données lemmatisées dans Pyrrha sont nettoyées avant la lemmatisation avec le script suivant : clean_prelematisation.Rmd

ici on utilise la lemmatisation automatisée avec cltk : cf notebook Lemmatisation_cltk/lem2_test.ipynb

4 comparer des dataset

#when we use a range of file have a main folder and all the file.txt inside : use this code
list_of_files <- list.files(path = "./Lambertus_Tim_1.2/", recursive = TRUE,
                            pattern = "\\.txt$", 
                            full.names = TRUE)
#install.packages("tidyverse", repos = "https://cran.rstudio.com")
#assuming tab separated values with a header    
datalist = lapply(list_of_files, function(x)paste(scan(x, what="character", sep="", fileEncoding="UTF-8"),collapse=" "))
#save the file for control
fileConn<-file("corpus_clean.txt")
writeLines(as.character(datalist), fileConn)
close(fileConn)

5 nettoyage des données

5.1 donnée pyrrha

on travail avec un fichier tsv contenant un texte lemmatiser avec Pyrrha: * on doit recréer le texte à partir de tsv

# Define a list (or vector) of file paths to your lemmatized TSV files
datalist <- c("Aretius_Tim_1.1-6/Caput_2/aretius-2_lemmatized.txt")  # add more file paths if needed
increment <- 0
mybiglist <- list()
for(file_path in datalist){  
  # Read the TSV file (adjust header and separator if needed)
  x <- read.delim(file_path, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)  
  textLemmat <- ""
  if(nrow(x) != 0){
    # Extract the first lemma token
    textLemmat <- x$lemma[1]    
    # Loop through the remaining rows/tokens
    for(i in 2:nrow(x)){
      if(!is.na(x$lemma[i])){
        textLemmat <- paste(textLemmat, x$lemma[i], sep = " ")
      }
    }
  }  
  increment <- increment + 1
  mybiglist[[increment]] <- textLemmat
}
corpus_lemmatised <- mybiglist
corpus_lemmatised[[1]][1]

5.2 donnée cltk

On travaille avec un text déjà lemmatisées avec cltk

# Define a list of file paths
datalist <- c("Lambertus_Tim_1.2/Lamb_chap_2_lematized.txt")  # Add more file paths if needed

increment <- 0
mybiglist <- list()

for(file_path in datalist){
  
  # Read the content of the file
  text_data <- readLines(file_path, warn = FALSE)  # Read the file into a character vector
  
  # Combine the lines into one single text string
  text_combined <- paste(text_data, collapse = " ")

  increment <- increment + 1
  mybiglist[[increment]] <- text_combined

}

# Store the result in corpus_lemmatised
corpus_lemmatised <- mybiglist

# Display the first element
corpus_lemmatised[[1]]

Chorinth. . versus . sic conuerto hic suus in is iudicium dominus in is ipse consolatio et salus vias , dum hic subiectio erga maritus vocatio is proprius sum statuo . in qui ille primus sum obseruo vox non denoto hic locus causa efficiens : sed medius tantum , per qui , tamquam per iter ab deus demonstro , sum ille pergo et progredior . in qui pecco papistus et pelagianus , omnisque operista , et quidem grauiter , qui salus noster causa in noster opus quaero et constituo . quis enim viduis , qui nullus liber vnquam suscipio : virgo , et is etiam qui cum sum coniux , nullus liber tamen pepereo , futurus sum ( vt recte hic locus chrysostus . animaduo ) si salus mulier totus pendeo ? Certe salua non facio . sed et thomas aquina hic deliro , dum laus virginitas et celibo cum hic paulus dico concilio , et placo nitor , quod cum ille aperte et perpiscue pugno . ergo hic vocatio et munus mulier describo etiam in is ipse , in qui poena suus peccatum sentio . sum autem , vt liber non tantum suscipio et gigno : sed vt educo , curo , et onus ille primus liber nutricatio , scero quidem molestus , lubeo volo deuo et suscipio . T enim hic locus non tantum parturitio ipse mulier significo : sed quisquis ille adiungo sum , et immineo iustus mater cura , vt liber edo educo . Vnde meritum mater puerpera damno , qui filius , si possum , suus non alo , qui Plutarchus in libus liber educatio . et dictum gregorius in canon n. ad is distinct. . mille quidem sum taedium , qui contra iouinia . enumero Hieronym . tam minus , vt ipse puerpera sum aliquando video , qui tamen perpetuo vico celebs . mille etiam dolor et molestia non tantum leuiter degusto : sed diute deuoro , tum in partus , tum post partus . qui tamen omnis si libeo et gratus animus deuo , atque suscipio mater , deus gratus sum , et in suus vocatio incedo : ad trimatus autem vsque lex ciuilis iubeo vt mater ipse alatcor liber suus , isquis praecipue curo . sed addo paulus alius quoque virtus , qui sum necessarius ostendo , vt mulier deus placeo , qui alius communis ille sum etiam cum vis , nempe fides , et Charitas : alius ille proprius , sanctificatio , et Modestia . qui enim virtus nos deus commendo sum fides . ille enim nos et deduco ad christus , et cum is coniungo . ille charitas quoque gigno , extra qui nihil ab mater ipse facio deus gratus possum , quia si inuitus , repugno , et cogo potius officium facio , quam ex charitas , displiceo deus . sanctificatio , qui requiro ab mulier , non sum tantum generalis omnis vitas actio ad deus voluntas conformatio . thess. . versus . sed magne sanctimonium quidam corpus , qui se vxor et mulier ab omnis turpitudo , immunditia , et lasciuia purus conseruo , qui impudicitie oppono : et alius nomen dico castitas . Modestia , luxuus et sumptuo ille cultus , qui supra dico , oppono .

6 premier nettoyage des données pour les coocurrences :

pour travailler sur les cooccurrences on conserve la puctuation qui permet de découper le document en phrase. * plus tard, il s’agira de le découper par verset.

#keep filename, get rid of the path
df<-df %>%
  mutate(document = word(document, -1, sep = "/"))
#remove punctuation
df$texteLemmat<-gsub('[[:punct:] ]+',' ',df$texteLemmat)
#remove numbers
df$texteLemmat<-gsub('[[:digit:] ]+',' ',df$texteLemmat)
print(df)

8 premières analyse de fréquence:

Un première examen des fréquences statistiques permet de visualiser les mots importants, de poser les bases d’un topic modeling. * pour l’instant on se concentre sur les fréquence de mots.

freq <- as.data.frame(colSums(as.matrix(dtm)))
colnames(freq) <- c("frequence")
#Je dessine mon graph
ggplot(freq, aes(x=frequence)) + geom_density()

# pour voir un historiogramme : 
#ggplot(freq, aes(x = frequence)) + geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "blue", alpha = 0.5)

12 script de nettoyage II

  • je supprime les mots non signifiant récurrents
  • je supprime tous les textes suvis d’un point directement pour enlever les abréviations.
# Define your stopwords list
MesStopWords <- c("que", "uel", "caput", "uersus", 
                  "versus", "quartus", "contra", "vt",
                   "locus", "siue", "liber", "libus",
                   "quemadmodum", "quanquam")

# Custom function to clean text
clean_text <- function(text) {
  # Remove words followed by a period
  text <- gsub("\\b\\w+\\.\\s*", "", text)
  text <-gsub("æ", "ae", text)
  # Remove stopwords (case insensitive)
  words <- unlist(strsplit(text, "\\s+"))
  words <- words[!tolower(words) %in% tolower(MesStopWords)]
  text <- paste(words, collapse = " ")
  return(text)
}

# Apply cleaning to your corpus_clean object
cleaned_text <- clean_text(as.character(corpus_clean))

# Save the cleaned file
fileConn <- file("corpus_clean_lemmatised.txt")
writeLines(cleaned_text, fileConn)
close(fileConn)

12.1 Co-occurrences

12.1.1 Pre-processing

We split the text into sentences (to create a context for the co-occurrences):

full_data <- readLines("corpus_clean_lemmatised.txt")

# Apply the normalization to each line
cleaned_data <- sapply(full_data, clean_text, USE.NAMES = FALSE)

writeLines(cleaned_data, "corpus_clean_lemmatised.txt")
# Inspect the result
head(full_data, 1)  # Show the first line of the cleaned text

12.1.1.1 Split the text in to sentences

ajout de point pour découper le texte

library(stringr)

# Read the text file
full_data <- readLines("corpus_clean_lemmatised.txt")  
full_text <- paste(full_data, collapse = " ")  # Combine into a single string

# Split into words
words <- unlist(str_split(full_text, "\\s+"))  # Split on whitespace
words <- words[words != ""]  # Remove empty entries (if any)

# Determine where to insert dots
n_words <- length(words)
split_points <- seq(15, n_words, by = 15)  # Positions to insert dots

# Insert a dot every 15 words
if (length(split_points) > 0) {
  for (i in rev(split_points)) {  # Reverse to avoid shifting indices
    if (i < n_words) {  # Avoid adding a dot at the very end if not needed
      words <- append(words, ".", after = i)
    }
  }
}

# Reconstruct the text
new_text <- paste(words, collapse = " ")

# Remove potential double dots or spaces around dots
new_text <- str_replace_all(new_text, "\\.\\.+", ".")  # Fix multiple dots
new_text <- str_replace_all(new_text, "\\s\\.\\s", " . ")  # Ensure space around dots

# Write back to file (or inspect)
writeLines(new_text, "corpus_with_dots_every_15_words.txt")
full_data <- readLines("corpus_with_dots_every_15_words.txt")


writeLines(cleaned_data, "corpus_with_dots_every_15_words.txt")
# Inspect the result
head(full_data, 1)  # Show the first line of the cleaned text

# read in and process text
full_data_sentences <- full_data %>%
  #remove useless whitespaces
  stringr::str_squish() %>%
  sbo::tokenize_sentences(.) %>%
  unlist() %>%
  stringr::str_remove_all("- ") %>%
  stringr::str_replace_all("\\W", " ") %>%
  stringr::str_squish()
# inspect data
head(full_data_sentences)
## [1] "cap adhortor facio deprecatio prex postulatio gratia actio uis homo Transitio euangelicus munus pars publicus"          
## [2] "precus quilibet homo genus conceptio profusio coram deus disputatio commode subicio suscipio argumentum pastor ecclesia"
## [3] "munus pars paulus informo superior conclusio bonus pietas christianus exercitium verus fides conseruo modus tutus"      
## [4] "prex impetro deus sanus doctrina metus pergo confirmo cresco paulus breuiter compleo quicumque oratio prex"             
## [5] "christianus quaero genus prex fundo Vbi quando animus reuerentia totus coetus decor singulus dominus tal"               
## [6] "do explico loquor imprimus paulus publicus ecclesia prex singulus christianus priuo precatio facio domus conclauus"
increment <- 1
mybiglist <- list()

# Process each sentence in the already lemmatized text
for (sentence in full_data_sentences) {
  textLemmat <- trimws(sentence)  # Remove extra spaces

  if (nchar(textLemmat) > 0) {  # Store only non-empty sentences
    mybiglist[[increment]] <- textLemmat
    increment <- increment + 1
  }
}

# Convert list to vector
full_data_sentences_lemmatised <- unlist(mybiglist)

# Show the last few sentences
tail(full_data_sentences_lemmatised)

# Load stopwords (ensure they're a vector)
stopword_enLigne <- read.csv("stopwords/latin_stop_word.csv", header=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
stopword_enLigne <- unlist(stopword_enLigne)  # Convert to vector

# Remove stopwords (ensure text is character)
full_data_sentences_lemmatised <- removeWords(full_data_sentences_lemmatised, stopword_enLigne)

# Optional: Remove extra whitespace
full_data_sentences_lemmatised <- stringr::str_squish(full_data_sentences_lemmatised)

I can download the data to correct it even more:

write.table(full_data_sentences_lemmatised, "full_data_sentences_lemmatised.txt")

And now I load the corrected data:

full_data_sentences_lemmatised <- readLines("full_data_sentences_lemmatised.txt", encoding="UTF-8")
empty_lines = grepl('^\\s*$', full_data_sentences_lemmatised)
full_data_sentences_lemmatised = full_data_sentences_lemmatised[! empty_lines]
#full_data_sentences_lemmatised = paste(full_data_sentences_lemmatised, collapse = '\n')
grep("^$", full_data_sentences_lemmatised)
## integer(0)
text_dfm <- full_data_sentences_lemmatised %>% 
  quanteda::tokens(remove_punct = TRUE)  %>%
  dfm() %>%
  #quanteda::dfm_remove(stopwords('italian'))%>%
  #quanteda::dfm_remove(c("almeno", "via")) %>%
  quanteda::dfm_trim(min_termfreq = 10, verbose = FALSE)
# inspect
text_dfm[1:6, 1:6]

text_dfm <- full_data_sentences_lemmatised %>% 
  quanteda::tokens(remove_punct = TRUE) %>%
  dfm() %>%
  quanteda::dfm_trim(
    min_termfreq = 5,       # Keep terms appearing ≥5 times
    max_docfreq = 0.5,      # Remove terms in >50% of docs
    docfreq_type = "prop",  # Proportional threshold
    min_docfreq = 0.01      # NEW: Keep terms in ≥1% of docs (optional)
  )

Regarder quels termes on a éliminer au cours du nettoyage des données pour vérifier qu’il s’agit bien de mot inutile ou de bruit.

# Original DFM before trimming
original_dfm <- full_data_sentences_lemmatised %>% 
  quanteda::tokens(remove_punct = TRUE) %>%
  dfm()

# Get removed terms (terms in original but not in trimmed)
removed_terms <- setdiff(featnames(original_dfm), featnames(text_dfm))
head(removed_terms, 20)  # View first 20 removed terms

##  [6] "postulatio" "uis"        "transitio"  "2"          "precus"

14 Visualiser le resultat avec un Worldcloud

library(quanteda.textplots)
textplot_wordcloud(text_dfm, max_words = 50)

14.1 Ameliorer la visualisation

textplot_wordcloud(
  text_dfm,
  max_words = 50,
  color = c("#6f7f81", "#2081f0", "darkblue"),  # Custom color gradient
  random_order = FALSE,                     # Disable random placement
  rotation = 0.25,                         # 25% of words rotated (for aesthetics)
  font = "sans"                           # Change font (try "sans", "serif", "mono")
)

14.2 Choosing a word

  1. on choisit un mot pour analyser ses co-occurrence
coocTerm <- "mulier"
  1. on compte les termes co-occurrent :
coocCounts <- t(text_dfm) %*% text_dfm
dim(coocCounts) # to check the matrix dimension
## [1] 264 264
as.matrix(coocCounts[15:17, 15:17])
##             features
## features     argumentum pastor ecclesia
##   argumentum          7      1        3
##   pastor              1     16        8
##   ecclesia            3      8       63
text_dfm_trimmed <- dfm_trim(text_dfm, min_termfreq = 5)  # Example: keep terms appearing ≥5 times
coocCounts <- t(text_dfm_trimmed) %*% text_dfm_trimmed
coocCounts <- fcm(text_dfm, context = "document", count = "frequency")
# Convert to a full matrix (if it's sparse)
cooc_matrix <- as.matrix(coocCounts)

# Find top co-occurring pairs (excluding diagonal)
diag(cooc_matrix) <- 0  # Ignore self-co-occurrences
top_cooc <- sort(cooc_matrix, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]  # Top 10
print(top_cooc)
##  [1] 46 40 31 29 28 24 21 20 20 18
# Get all co-occurrences for "mulier"
#mulier_cooc <- sort(coocCounts["mulier", ], decreasing = TRUE)
#head(mulier_cooc, 10)  # Top 10 co-occurring words

15 Network visualisation

library(igraph)
# Convert to a graph (ignoring low-frequency edges)
graph <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(coocCounts, weighted = TRUE, mode = "undirected")
## Warning: The `adjmatrix` argument of `graph_from_adjacency_matrix()` must be symmetric
## with mode = "undirected" as of igraph 1.6.0.
## ℹ Use mode = "max" to achieve the original behavior.
## This warning is displayed once every 8 hours.
## Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was
## generated.
# Simplify (remove loops and multiple edges)
graph <- simplify(graph)
# Plot the graph
plot(graph, edge.width = E(graph)$weight, vertex.label.cex = 0.7)

# Keep only edges with weight >= threshold (e.g., 5)
graph <- graph_from_adjacency_matrix(
  coocCounts, 
  weighted = TRUE, 
  mode = "undirected"
)
graph <- delete_edges(graph, E(graph)[E(graph)$weight < 5])  # Adjust threshold
graph <- simplify(graph)  # Remove loops
graph <- delete_vertices(graph, V(graph)[degree(graph) == 0])
plot(graph, 
     edge.width = E(graph)$weight / max(E(graph)$weight) * 3,  # Scale edge width
     vertex.size = 5,                                         # Smaller nodes
     vertex.label.cex = 0.6,                                  # Smaller labels
     vertex.color = "lightblue",                              # Node color
     layout = layout_with_fr(graph))                          # Force-directed layout

subgraph <- make_ego_graph(graph, order = 1, nodes = "mulier")[[1]]
plot(subgraph, 
     edge.width = E(subgraph)$weight / max(E(subgraph)$weight) * 3,
     vertex.label.cex = 0.7)

16 interactive visualisation

for an interactive visualisation use visNetwork : more information https://datastorm-open.github.io/visNetwork/

library(visNetwork)
nodes <- data.frame(id = V(graph)$name, label = V(graph)$name)
edges <- data.frame(from = ends(graph, E(graph))[,1], 
                    to = ends(graph, E(graph))[,2],
                    width = E(graph)$weight)
visNetwork(nodes, edges) %>% 
  visOptions(highlightNearest = TRUE, nodesIdSelection = TRUE)

17 cibler sur mulier

library(visNetwork)

# 1. Convert the subgraph to visNetwork format
nodes <- data.frame(
  id = V(subgraph)$name,
  label = V(subgraph)$name,
  title = V(subgraph)$name,  # Tooltip on hover
  value = degree(subgraph),  # Node size by degree
  color = "#b3ade6"        # Customize color
)

edges <- data.frame(
  from = ends(subgraph, E(subgraph))[, 1],
  to = ends(subgraph, E(subgraph))[, 2],
  width = E(subgraph)$weight / max(E(subgraph)$weight) * 10,  # Scale edge width
  smooth = TRUE  # Curved edges
)

# 2. Create interactive plot
visNetwork(nodes, edges) %>%
  visNodes(font = list(size = 20)) %>%
  visEdges(selectionWidth = 2) %>%
  visOptions(
    highlightNearest = list(enabled = TRUE, degree = 1, hover = TRUE),
    nodesIdSelection = TRUE  # Dropdown menu to select nodes
  ) %>%
  visLayout(randomSeed = 42)  # For consistent layout
